chapter: Coltrane, Jimmy Smith and musical values
title: Discography talk and closing of day one
summary: They discuss unlisted non-jazz sessions and agree to continue tomorrow.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: Well, I want to go back again because when I look at your. Do we have a minute?
Like one more minute, or a couple of minutes.

Okay, well again, so what I’d like to do is when we are able to resume is you were so prolific, I know they weren’t all the sessions you liked, but during that period from ’56 to ’60, lets just say up to ’61 before you got the pit orchestra gig. You were working with everybody, so I want to talk about your experiences, your first two guitar recording with Freddie Green.
Oh yeah, that’s great. But you know what this guy, the thing that…
This thing, whatever you got there, the jazz thing. I bet there’s a lot more that’s not even in there.
On sessions I was on that are not even listed because they were not jazz.

He has the James Brown on there, Wynonie Harris. And like I said, he’s got a lot, I looked down there and I was saying, “Kenny is in the studio every week with somebody else.” I mean, March of ’57 you were just bam, bam, bam. And then some days were double I’m looking at the date and you’re doing two sessions. Like you mentioned the one with Red Garland.
Right, and it’s completely different genres, you were all over the map and you were impacting music, so maybe we can just touch on that tomorrow and pick up with the rest of the career in the 60’s.
Okay, I really need to get a hold of that though, if you help me with that I’d really appreciate it.
I guess we should wrap it up maybe.
Well, you know, yeah, lets go ahead, but I mean, but we’re still going to continue tomorrow?
